objectives: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of various analgesic therapies for managing rheumatoid arthritis-related pain symptoms.
inclusion_criteria: Adult patients (18+) diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis experiencing disease-related pain; human studies only. Studies had to assess the effectiveness of analgesic treatments, including pharmaceutical therapies (NSAIDs, opioids, acetaminophen/paracetamol, COX-2 inhibitors, biologics, corticosteroids) and non-pharmaceutical therapies (physical therapy, neural training, functional training, occupational therapy, ergotherapy, cognitive behavioral therapy, hypnotherapy, ultrasound therapy, acupuncture, thermotherapy, laser therapy, electrotherapy, balneotherapy). Eligible comparisons included drug versus drug, drug versus non-pharmaceutical intervention, drug versus placebo, non-pharmaceutical versus non-pharmaceutical, and non-pharmaceutical versus placebo. Outcomes had to relate to pain relief, pain management, pain severity scores, reduction of pain intensity, or maintenance of pain symptoms. All study durations and follow-ups were eligible. Eligible designs were randomized controlled trials, cohort studies (prospective and retrospective), and case-controlled studies. No publication-date limits were applied; English-language articles and English abstracts of non-English articles were reviewed.
exclusion_criteria: Patients with non-rheumatoid-arthritis-related pain; mixed patient populations where rheumatoid-arthritis-specific data were not clearly distinguished; studies focused on treatments unrelated to pain management or not using analgesic therapies, including DMARDs that do not primarily target pain; studies without a comparison between treatments or interventions; studies that did not report pain-related outcomes; case series, case reports, editorials, opinion pieces, letters, animal studies, in vitro studies, and abstracts without a published study manuscript. The Methods section also states that studies were excluded if they were non-comparative, involved non-human subjects, or if pain outcomes could not be clearly attributed to active rheumatoid arthritis without other comorbidities affecting pain relief.

selection_evidence: Results/Fig. 1 report 303 records identified, 271 after deduplication, 81 full texts assessed, 17 unretrieved, 38 excluded, and 26 studies retained for the final systematic analysis. Table 3 lists 26 study-characteristic entries, and those entries map to references 11-36. The only numbering anomaly is Emery et al., shown as [32] in Table 3; the reference list identifies Emery as ref 30 and Kawai as ref 32, so the included-study set is the contiguous literature range 11-36. The subgroup Results are also consistent with this set: 5-point refs 12-17, 10-point refs 18-22, and 100-point refs 11 and 23-36.
notes: The manuscript distinguishes 26 included studies in the final systematic analysis from only 17 treatment regimens with sufficient quantitative data for pooling. I returned the 26-study included-study set because Table 3 is the explicit included-studies table used by the workflow. Table 2 also states case series were excluded, but Table 3/Results include two prospective case series (refs 20 and 24).
